findings.description: AC-4 says 'GET /a%2Fb?q=%20 reaches req.rawPath() = /a%2Fb'. An encoded slash is rejected by the wave 2 validator: PathValidator.isValid decodes 'a%2Fb' to 'a/b' and returns false (seg.indexOf('/') >= 0), so the dispatcher answers 400 before any Request exists (FR-HTTP-002 AC-3/AC-4; residual 'Pre-request rejections'; carried-into-wave-5.md: 'an encoded slash is rejected with 400 by D-052'). The AC contradicts verified FR-ROUTE-004 and cannot pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an allowed encoded segment, e.g. 'GET /a%20b?q=%20 reaches req.rawPath() = /a%20b and raw query q=%20 (req.query("q") = " ")'.

findings.description: AC-7: 'express-migration.md maps req.originalUrl to req.rawPath() described as req.path before decoding'. The wave decision (Remaining markers) says: 'The Express counterpart of rawPath() becomes "req.path before decoding" (not req.originalUrl, which includes the query)'. AC-1 of the same requirement also says 'not req.originalUrl'. Keeping the row `req.originalUrl` -> `req.rawPath()` (express-migration.md:46) contradicts both.
findings.suggested_fix: Make AC-7 require that express-migration.md no longer maps req.originalUrl to req.rawPath(): the rawPath() row names 'req.path before decoding', and the req.originalUrl row (if kept) points to rawPath() plus the query string through req.query(...), or is marked as having no direct counterpart, with no marker.

findings.description: AC-5 needs 'a path with only a WebSocket route' to get 426 through the harness (D-395, T06, D-397). Wave 3 has no way to register one. IR-HTTP-005 AC-5 makes the wave 3 RestApp methods 'exactly the route registration and routing policy methods above', and that list has no ws(...). FR-HTTP-008 builds the Router only at freeze, from registrations the app recorded, so a test cannot call Router.addWebSocket directly. No requirement names a harness or internal hook that registers a WebSocket route, and the dispatcher's handling of a MATCHED result with RouteKind.WEBSOCKET is not stated. As written, the AC cannot be done.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC (FR-HTTP-008 or FR-HTTP-001) for an internal registration hook on the internal RestApp implementation, used by the harness, that records a WebSocket route for the freeze (e.g. 'the harness registers a WebSocket-only route through the internal implementation, not a public RestApp method'). State that wave 3 never dispatches an upgrade to that route (or what it answers) until wave 8.

findings.description: AC-9: 'Every docs/api Java example whose methods exist at the wave 3 merge compiles in the docs-example test set'. No docs-example test set exists in the repo (only RoutingDocsTest and BuildLayoutTest read docs/api). I-009 puts it in 'the root test suite'. The AC does not say how snippets are extracted and wrapped (most are fragments such as `res.status(204).end();`), which files are in scope, or how 'whose methods exist' is decided. Two testers could reach different verdicts.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the mechanism and set: e.g. 'a root test extracts each ```java fence of docs/api/{request,response,routing,app}.md, wraps it in a handler/method template with req, res, app in scope, and compiles it; fences that reference a method absent at the wave 3 merge (json, use, builder, cookie, body, form, file, ws, ...) are listed in an explicit exclusion list in the test'.

findings.description: AC-3: 'acquiring the body through BodyState for a JSON, form, multipart or raw read after a first read of any kind gets BodyAlreadyConsumedException'. Read literally, a form read after a form read must throw. AC-4 (D-087) requires repeated form/multipart reads to share one parse 'without BodyAlreadyConsumedException'. D-086 says the shared parse is 'the only exemption', but AC-3 leaves the exemption out, so the two ACs contradict each other.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC-3 to say: '... after a first read of a different kind, or a second JSON or raw read, gets BodyAlreadyConsumedException; the shared form/multipart parse of AC-4 is the only exemption'.

findings.description: The ACs require 'a test with a router spy', a 'validator spy', and 'a test handler registered on every path' / 'registered routes on every path'. Router is 'public final class Router<H>' and PathValidator is a final class with a static isValid. The test classpath has only JUnit 4, no mocking library. RoutePattern.parse rejects '*', so no pattern matches every path. The SRS does not require the seam that would make these spies possible.
findings.suggested_fix: Either require an internal seam (the dispatcher takes its lookup and validator as package-private interfaces that tests replace), or restate the ACs by observable outcome: a handler on '/' and '/:x' records no call, and the outcome is 400/204/501 even with routes that would otherwise match.

findings.description: 'answered 400 without a router lookup and without decoding the path first' has no observable test for 'without decoding the path first'.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the clause or make it observable: e.g. '/a%2e%2e' and '/a%2Fb' are rejected with 400, while '/a%252e' is accepted (validator on the raw form, single decoding).

findings.description: 'The malformed-query 400 is produced after the Request object exists' cannot be observed in wave 3. There is no middleware or onError, and the handler is not called (AC-3).
findings.suggested_fix: Turn it into a design note, or give an observable form, e.g. 'a dispatcher unit test with an injected request factory records one Request built for ?x=%zz and none for a validator-rejected path'.

findings.description: 'a counting stream shows no single read larger than a fixed buffer bound': the bound is not named, so a test cannot decide pass or fail. The rationale says 'No chunk size is fixed here'.
findings.suggested_fix: Let the test read the bound from an internal constant ('no read requests more than DefaultResponse.COPY_BUFFER bytes and that constant is <= 64 KiB'), or state 'every read(byte[],int,int) call requests fewer bytes than the 1 MiB input'.

findings.description: AC-4 says 'the stream rejects the body before reading any byte' but does not say how: an exception at construction or on the first read, and of which type. AC-3 says 'fails on the read' without a type. Waves 5 and 6 must map the failure to 413, so the failure needs a type they can recognise. The requirement also does not say how the stream learns the declared Content-Length.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the constructor inputs (limit, optional declared length) and the failure: e.g. 'throws an internal BodyTooLargeException (an IOException) on the first read when the declared length > limit, and on the read that would return byte limit+1'.

findings.description: AC-3: 'a test against the in-memory adapter reads the bound port right after the bind call returns'. The in-memory adapter has no socket, and the AC gives no expected value, so pass/fail is open. AC-2 needs a core-owned event-stream drain loop running in an in-memory test in wave 3, while res.sse and its core arrive in wave 7. The AC does not say which core component supplies the loop in wave 3.
findings.suggested_fix: AC-3: state the expected value (e.g. the in-memory adapter reports the requested port, or a fixed non-zero port for port 0). AC-2: allow a test-supplied drain loop against the SPI type, or state which wave 3 core component (e.g. stream()) uses it.

findings.description: 'a test in another module that depends on the NaruServe-api test fixtures can use it' is not in D-108 ('ship an in-memory HttpAdapter in a test fixtures source set'). No module declares testFixtures(project(':NaruServe-api')) today, so this adds an unrequested build change.
findings.suggested_fix: Reduce it to: the class is in NaruServe-api/src/testFixtures/java, is in the test-fixtures jar (CON-BUILD-006 AC-8), and NaruServe-api's own tests use it. Or name the consuming module and the build.gradle change explicitly.

findings.description: D-100 (throw after commit) is tested only 'after res.send("a") committed the response'. send() also completes the response, so this case is the same as D-084's completion case (FR-HTTP-018 AC-1). No AC tests status or header while COMMITTED/STREAMING but not COMPLETED.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'during res.stream(...) (state STREAMING), res.status(500) and res.header("X","1") throw an exception and the sent status and headers stay unchanged'.

findings.description: 'app.route(...) registration ... throw IllegalStateException' is ambiguous. route(String) returns a RouteBuilder, and the AC does not say whether app.route(path) itself throws after the freeze or the builder's get(h) does, including a builder obtained before the freeze.
findings.suggested_fix: State both: app.route(Method/MethodSet, path, h) throws, and RouteBuilder.get/put/... throw after the freeze even on a builder obtained before it (app.route(path) may also throw).

findings.description: The Rationale is '-'. Hygiene requires the rationale to list the covered D-ids: D-070, D-038, D-109, D-398 and residual r5 W2-001 (supersede of OPS-ROUTE-001).
findings.suggested_fix: Rationale: 'Covers D-070, D-038, D-109, D-398 and wave-3 residual r5 W2-001; supersedes OPS-ROUTE-001, restating AC-1/AC-2 and AC-3 for the wave 3 marker set.'

findings.ac: AC-5; IR-HTTP-001 AC-3; FR-HTTP-019 AC-5; FR-HTTP-003 AC-1..AC-5 empty body
findings.description: Several ACs that will become verified state wave-3 snapshots without a wave scope in the AC text: RestApp methods 'exactly' those of wave 3, 'no method named body/json/...', 'no public body-reading method', and 404/405/426/501 with an empty body (the FR-HTTP-003 requirement statement has no 'until wave 4'). Wave 4 (use, listen, error body) and wave 5 (body, json) will fail these verified tests, which is a regression trap under I-014's additive model.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope each snapshot AC explicitly ('at the wave 3 merge', 'until wave 4 adds the standard error body', as FR-HTTP-006 does), or phrase them as 'only the methods of D-392's later waves are absent', so later waves supersede them deliberately.

findings.req_id: IR-HTTP-001, CON-HTTP-001, FR-HTTP-001, FR-HTTP-002, FR-HTTP-003, IR-HTTP-005, IR-HTTP-006, FR-HTTP-008, OPS-HTTP-001
findings.description: 11 Code trace rows use 'uses | trace_intent=verifies' (Method.java, build.gradle x2, Router.java x2, PathValidator.java, RouteMatch.java, RouterPolicy.java, RoutingConfigException.java, RoutePattern.java, RoutingDocsTest.java) rather than trace_intent=addition_site. They point at existing files, so this is defensible, but it does not follow the requested convention.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep them as Requirement/depends_on links or mark them as intentional non-addition traces if the convention allows; otherwise use addition_site only for files the wave edits (RoutingDocsTest.java is edited).

findings.description: 'signatures reference only java.* types and com.snoworca.naruserve types': this excludes the org.jspecify annotations that IR-HTTP-001 AC-4 requires on signatures. It also allows java.nio.file / java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture / java.net.http, which I-003 forbids (animal-sniffer would catch most of them).
findings.suggested_fix: '... only java.* (excluding java.nio.file, CompletableFuture, java.net.http), com.snoworca.naruserve and org.jspecify annotation types'.

findings.description: 'Wave 3 tests of automatic responses assert status and headers only, plus the empty body' is a rule for writing tests, not observable system behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Move it to Implementation Notes, or drop it, since AC-1..AC-5 already fix what is asserted.

findings.description: The wave decision 'Automatic response bodies' gives the automatic 400 an empty body with Content-Length: 0. FR-HTTP-005 AC-3 asserts this for non-'/' paths, but no AC asserts it for the validator-rejection 400.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'with Content-Length: 0 and an empty body' to FR-HTTP-002 AC-3.

findings.description: AC-8 lists the markers that stay as 'file disposition and redirect in response.md, proxy trust and parts() in request.md, RouteBuilder.use in routing.md'. request.md also has the jsonTree()/jsonMap() marker, and express-migration.md has many markers owned by other issues (trust proxy, Router mount, res.type, cors, ...). The list reads as complete when it is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Phrase it as 'markers other than those listed in the requirement stay, including ...'.

findings.description: 'the header names and values in received order' is not in D-105, which only says 'headers'. It is harmless but adds a constraint the sources do not state.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep it with a note that it derives from D-079 (first value / every value), or drop 'in received order'.

findings.description: Only the marker test is planned to re-cite the successor. The RoutingDocsTest tests sdsAc10_OPS_ROUTE_001_AC1 and sdsAc9_OPS_ROUTE_001_AC2 still cite the discarded OPS-ROUTE-001, while OPS-ROUTE-002 restates those ACs.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the worker re-cite all three RoutingDocsTest tests to OPS-ROUTE-002 AC-1/AC-2/AC-3 (the trace link already names the file).
